The name `copy-general` is a NEUTRAL WORKING NAME: the owner has not yet named this chain (I-82, copy-machine participation) and the build's ruling is that the name is his to pick and is not `copy` (stdlib shadow). Renaming is one `git mv` of this folder plus this file's `chain` field. `sha` and every pick's `sha256` are filled BY THE RESOLVER at resolve time; a pick digest that is absent has not been resolved yet, and the declared test fails by name until it is.
gaps: THE SUBSTITUTE HALF OF HIS LANE OVERLAY. His runner does two things on the triaged lane: it SKIPS stage6 when the lane is not ORGANIC, and it then feeds stage7's `body` the EXPANSION output when stage6 ran and the INJECTION output when it did not. CR-5's `when:` gave the skip a form; the substitute has none — a gate decides WHETHER a stage runs, never which input another stage reads, and there is no conditional-input form in schema 1. This chain therefore binds `body` to `@stage3`, the value his runner uses on every non-ORGANIC run and the one that always exists, and an ORGANIC run here hands stage7 the injection where his hands it the expansion. This is the same overlay the video-teardown pin recorded as unpinned follow-on scope; it is the first thing CM-2's goldens will show on an ORGANIC run, and the redesign signal it may raise is a chain-runner extension question, not a prompt-tuning one.

HIS stage1b READS TWO STAGE OUTPUTS CONCATENATED. copy.py passes `concept_brief=f"{triage}\n\n{spec}"` — one prompt token fed by two earlier stages joined by a blank line. `inputs` binds one reference per name and there is no concat form, so this chain takes `concept_brief` as `@config.concept_brief`, which a caller (and CM-2's harness) fills with exactly that join. It fails loudly and by name when nobody supplies it, which is the right failure: the alternative bindings either drop the spec silently or invent a twelfth stage this resolution did not find in his code.

THE PER-STAGE LANGUAGE QUERY IS NOT EXECUTED BY THIS ENGINE. Five stages take a `{language}` block that his runner produces by calling the language layer per stage (`L.for_stage(brand, <stage>, avatar, funnel, ...)`). This engine calls one thing, the model seam, and does not run queries, so each of those blocks arrives as its own run-config variable — `language_injection`, `language_hooks`, `language_expansion`, `language_close`, `language_render`. WHAT each stage asks the layer for is a chain definition and it lives beside this file, in `language-profile.json`, in the component's own chain-profile schema; the caller runs the query with that profile and passes the rendered blocks in. Nothing about the definition is lost — only the calling of it moves out.

AN UNREAD LANE FAILS HERE AND DEGRADES THERE. `lane` is a declared field, so a stage0 output with no LANE line fails stage0 by name. His runner records the lane as `unread` and carries on into a non-ORGANIC run. Failing is the ruled behaviour for an extracted field a later stage routes on; it is written down because it is a real difference in what a bad triage does.
